#Inpatient ## Diabetes-Related Foot Infections (Diabetic Foot Infections-DFI)
## Infected DFI (Class 3/Moderate)
Infection with no systemic manifestations and envolving:
-Erythema extending >2cm from the wound margin, and/or
-Tissue deeper than skin and subcutaneous tissues
(e.g., tendon, muscle, joint, and bone)
## Duration of therapy: 1-3 weeks
## Preferred Treatments:
**Oral options**
**IV options**
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h ($) [M] <AND> Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h ($) [DI,H]
## Treatment with MRSA risk factors:
**Oral options**
Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO q12h ($) [R] <AND> Trimethoprim-
sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet po q12h ($) [R,DI]
< OR >
PO BID for 14 days ($) [DI]
**IV options**
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h ($) [M] <AND> Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h ($) [DI,H]
<AND> Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]
< OR >
Ampicillin-sulbactam 3 gm IV q6h ($) [R] <AND> Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV
q12h ($) [R,DI]
## Treatment with Penicillin Allergy:
**Oral options**
**IV options**
($) [DI,H]
## Outpatient

## DIABETES-RELATED FOOT INFECTIONS (DIABETIC FOOT INFECTIONS-DFI)
## Wound Cultures:
If there are no systemic symptoms of infection or at least 2 local symptoms
(pain, erythema > 0.5cm, purulent drainage, warmth), do not culture or treat
with abx.
Do NOT:
-Culture a wound that appears uninfected (at least 2 of following: local pain,
erythema >0.5cm, purulent drainage)
-Swab the wound to obtain a culture
-Culture without first cleaning and debriding a wound DFI Do:
-Obtain culture by deep tissue biopsy after cleaning and debriding the wound
## Imaging:
-An x-ray is recommended for all new foot ulcers in patients with diabetes to
evaluate for deformity, bony destruction, soft tissue gas, and/or foreign
bodies. Antimicrobials aren't indicated unless local cellulitis or systemic
infectious symptoms are present.

## Uninfected DFI (Class 1/Uninfected): Chronic ulceration without s/s infection
-if no pain, erythema > 0.5cm, purulent drainage, do not culture or treat
Do not culture wound -Do not treat with antibiotics If osteomyelitis identified
arrange for bone biopsy --hold antibiotics

## Infected DFI (Class 2/Mild):
At least two of the following are present: -Local swelling or induration
-Erythema >0.5cm but <2cm around wound -Local tenderness or pain -Local
increased warmth -Purulent drainage
## Primarily Outpatient Treatment:
Duration of therapy: 1-2 weeks
## Preferred Regimens:
Cefadroxil 1000 mg PO q12h x 7days [R]
Non-VA order for above
< OR >
Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO BID for 7 days [R]
Non-VA order for above
## Treatment with previous MRSA infection or severe PCN allergy:
Beta-lactam Reaction Assessment
Trimethoprim sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO bid x 7days [R,DI]
Non-VA order for above
< OR >
Linezolid 600 mg PO BID for 7 days [DI,O]
Non-VA order for above

Infection with associated systemic manifestations as indicated by 2 or more of
the following: -Fever, Tachycardia, Leukocytosis, Hypotension, Sepsis,
Necrotizing infection

## Infected DFI (Class 4/Severe):
Infection with associated systemic manifestations as indicated by 2 or more of
the following: -Fever, Tachycardia, Leukocytosis, Hypotension, Sepsis,
Necrotizing infection
Duration: usually 2-4 weeks, unless source control/amputation occurs
Obtain cultures of inflamed ulcer or wound to permit targeted antimicrobial
therapy, de-escalate/modify regimen based on culture and susceptibility data. A
switch to an oral regimen is reasonable
Preferred:
Piperacillin-tazobactam 3.375 gm IV ONCE STAT [R] <AND> vancomycin
15 mg/kg IV ONCE STAT [R,DI]
< OR >
Cefepime 2 gm IV ONCE STAT [R] <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV
ONCE STAT [R,DI] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV ONCE STAT [DI]
Alternative:
Beta-lactam Reaction Assessment
Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV ONCE STAT [R] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV
ONCE STAT [DI] <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV ONCE STAT [R]
